intro: The Bible is full of people who had to be brave. In this unit you will meet a shepherd boy with a sling, a man in a den of lions, and a man inside a big fish. These stories come from the Old Testament, which Jews and Christians both read.

Then you will meet a teacher named Jesus. Christians tell his story from the New Testament. He taught with short stories called parables. You will hear about a lost sheep, a tiny seed and a hurt man on a road.
By the end, you will be able to tell each story in order, say who is in it, and say what a psalm, a prophet and a parable are. You will also learn what Christians remember at Christmas and Easter.
bigQuestion: What do these stories say about being brave and being kind?

timeline.t: David watches his family's sheep near Bethlehem
David faces the giant Goliath with a sling
David becomes king and makes Jerusalem his city
Songs called psalms carry David's name
Daniel prays and is thrown to the lions
Jonah runs away, meets a big fish, and goes to Nineveh
Luke and Matthew tell of a baby born in Bethlehem
Jesus teaches with parables like the lost sheep
Jesus tells the story of the Good Samaritan
Jesus welcomes the children his helpers sent away
Christians remember Jesus at Christmas and Easter

words.d: a person who watches sheep and keeps them safe
a strip of cloth or leather used to throw a stone fast
a song or poem from the Bible's book of Psalms
a person in the Bible who speaks a message the text says comes from God
doing the right thing even when you feel scared
one of four books that tell the story of Jesus
a short story with a lesson inside
a person near you who you should care about

test.q: What was David's job when he was a boy?
test.why: The story in 1 Samuel says David watched his family's sheep.

test.q: Who did David beat with a sling and a stone?
test.why: The story says David's stone hit the giant Goliath, and he fell.
Psalm 23 begins, "The LORD is my shepherd," and talks about green grass and quiet water.

test.q: Why was Daniel thrown to the lions?
test.why: The story says a rule said not to pray to anyone but the king, and Daniel prayed anyway.

test.q: What did the people of Nineveh do when Jonah spoke?
choices: They threw him in the sea
test.why: The book of Jonah says the whole city said sorry and changed.

choices: A person who speaks a message
test.why: In the Bible, a prophet speaks a message the text says comes from God. Jonah was one.

test.q: Which part of the Bible tells the story of Jesus?
test.why: The New Testament, with its four Gospels, tells the story of Jesus.

test.q: Which Gospel tells about the wise men and the star?
test.why: Matthew has the wise men and the star. Luke has the shepherds and the manger.

test.q: In the Good Samaritan story, what did the Samaritan do?
test.why: The priest and the temple helper walked past. The Samaritan stopped and cared for the man.

test.q: Which of these is a parable?
test.why: The lost sheep is a parable, a short story with a lesson, that the Gospels say Jesus told.

write.prompt: Pick one brave person from this unit: David, Daniel, Jonah or the Samaritan. Tell what the story says he did. Name the book the story is in, like 1 Samuel 17 or Luke 10. Then say why you think it was brave or kind.
tips: Say the book the story comes from.
Say "the story says" when you tell what happened.
Tell what happened in order: first, next, last.
Use a word from this unit, like prophet, psalm or parable.

title: Kings, Prophets and a Teacher

chapters.title: David, Daniel and Jonah
chapters.bigQuestion: What does it look like to be brave in these old stories?

story.title: Five Smooth Stones
story.kicker: A boy who watches sheep walks up to a giant with a sling in his hand.
paragraphs: Two armies stand on two hills. A valley sits between them. Every day a giant named Goliath walks out. He is very tall and wears heavy armor. He shouts, "Send someone to fight me!" Nobody wants to go.
A boy named David comes with bread for his brothers. He is a shepherd. He hears the giant shout. He sees the soldiers hide. The story says David asks, "Why is everyone afraid?"
David goes to King Saul. He says he will fight. Saul gives him armor, but it is too big. David takes it off. He walks to a stream and picks up five smooth stones. He puts them in his bag.
Goliath laughs at the boy. David does not run. He puts one stone in his sling. He swings it around and lets go. The story says the stone hits the giant, and the giant falls down.
story.think: David was small and the giant was big. Why do you think David was not afraid?

lessons.title: A Boy Who Watched Sheep
lessons.mainIdea: The story says David was the youngest son, and he watched sheep before he was a king.
reading: The Bible has a book called 1 Samuel. It tells a story about a boy named David. David lived in a town called Bethlehem. He had seven big brothers. His job was to watch the family's sheep.
A *shepherd* watches sheep. He keeps them safe from wild animals. He finds them grass and water. The story says David was a good shepherd. He was brave when a lion or a bear came.
One day a man named Samuel came to town. The story says God sent him to pick a new king. Samuel looked at all the big brothers. Then he asked for the youngest. The story says Samuel picked David.

words.d: a person who watches sheep and keeps them safe
the small town where the story says David grew up

look.title: Picture a Shepherd
look.text: Look at a green hill. Sheep are eating grass. One boy sits on a rock with a stick in his hand. He is watching. Far away, a bear comes out of the trees. The boy stands up. He is not big, but he does not run away.
look.prompt: What do you think the shepherd boy will do next? What makes a good shepherd?

check.q: What was David's job when he was a boy?
check.why: The story in 1 Samuel says David was a shepherd. He watched his family's sheep.

check.q: Where did David live?
check.why: The story says David's family lived in the town of Bethlehem.

check.q: Who came to town to pick a new king?
check.why: The story says Samuel came to Bethlehem. He looked at all the brothers and picked David.

lessons.title: David and the Giant
lessons.mainIdea: The story says David faced the giant Goliath with only a sling and a stone.
reading: Goliath was a soldier from the other army. The story says he was very tall. He had a big sword and a big spear. Every day he shouted for someone to fight him. The soldiers were afraid.
David was not a soldier. He was a shepherd boy. But the story says he was not afraid. He said he would fight. He did not wear armor. He took his sling and five smooth stones from a stream.
A *sling* is a strip of cloth or leather. You put a stone in it. You swing it fast and let go. The story says David's stone hit Goliath, and the giant fell. The soldiers cheered.

words.d: a strip of cloth or leather used to throw a stone fast
the very tall soldier the story says David beat with a sling

look.title: What David Said
look.text: The story says Goliath came at David with a sword and a spear. David told him: You come with a sword. I come in the name of God. Then David ran toward the giant.
look.cite: 1 Samuel 17:45–48, King James Version (1611), told in simple words
look.prompt: Goliath had a sword. What did David say he had? What do you think that means?

check.q: What did David use to fight Goliath?
check.why: The story says David took five smooth stones and his sling. He did not wear armor.

check.q: Why did nobody else fight Goliath?
check.why: The story says the soldiers were afraid of the tall giant. Only David said he would go.

check.q: Where did David get his stones?
check.why: The story says David picked five smooth stones out of a stream.

lessons.title: David Becomes King
lessons.mainIdea: The story says David grew up and became the king of Israel, with Jerusalem as his city.
reading: David grew up. The story says many people loved him. King Saul was jealous. David had to hide for a long time. But he did not hurt Saul. He waited.
After Saul died, the story says David became *king*. A king is the leader of a whole land. David made a city called *Jerusalem* his home. It became the most important city in the story.
The story says David was a good king, but not a perfect one. He made big mistakes. The story tells about them too. Jews and Christians both tell the story of King David.

words.d: the leader of a whole land
the city the story says King David made his home

look.title: From Sheep to a Crown
look.text: Think about David's life in order. First, a boy watching sheep. Next, a boy with a sling in front of a giant. Then, a young man hiding from a jealous king. Last, a king in Jerusalem. That is a long road for one person.
look.prompt: Which part of David's life would you pick to draw? Why that part?

check.q: What city did David make his home?
check.why: The story says David made Jerusalem his city when he was king.

check.q: Why did David have to hide?
check.why: The story says Saul was jealous of David. David hid, but he did not hurt Saul.

check.q: Which two groups tell the story of King David?
check.why: David's story is in the Hebrew Bible, which Jews read, and in the Old Testament, which Christians read.

lessons.title: Songs Called Psalms
lessons.mainIdea: The Bible has a book of songs called Psalms, and many of them have David's name at the top.
reading: The Bible has a book of songs. The songs are called *psalms*. There are 150 of them. Some are happy. Some are sad. Some say thank you. People still sing them today.
Many psalms have David's name at the top. Jewish and Christian tradition say David was a singer. The story says he played a harp. So people have long said David wrote many psalms.
Jews sing psalms at the synagogue. Christians sing psalms at church. Some people say a psalm at bedtime. A psalm can be said in any language.

words.d: a song or poem from the Bible's book of Psalms
a music tool with strings that the story says David played

look.title: Numbers in the Psalms
rows: Psalms with David's name at the top
look.cite: The book of Psalms, King James Version (1611); counts by the psalm headings
look.prompt: Which number is the biggest? Which psalm is the shortest?

check.q: What is a psalm?
choices: A song or poem from the Bible
check.why: A psalm is a song or poem. The book of Psalms has 150 of them.

check.q: How many psalms are in the book of Psalms?
check.why: The book of Psalms has 150 psalms.

check.q: Whose name is at the top of many psalms?
check.why: Many psalms have David's name at the top, and tradition says he was a singer.

lessons.title: Psalm 23 in Simple Words
lessons.mainIdea: Psalm 23 says God is like a shepherd who takes care of the singer.
reading: Psalm 23 is a very famous psalm. It is short. It has David's name at the top. It starts with the words, "The LORD is my shepherd." A shepherd takes care of sheep. The song says God is like that.
The psalm talks about green grass and quiet water. It talks about a dark valley. The singer walks through it and is not afraid. It ends with a house and a table full of food.
Many people say this psalm when they feel scared. Jews and Christians both know it well. It is read at happy times and sad times. You do not have to believe it to understand it.

words.d: a short, famous psalm that says God is like a shepherd

look.title: Psalm 23, Told Simply
look.text: God is my shepherd. I have what I need. He lets me rest in green grass. He leads me by quiet water. Even when I walk in a dark valley, I am not afraid, because he is with me.
look.cite: Psalm 23:1–4, King James Version (1611), told in simple words
look.prompt: The psalm calls God a shepherd. What does a shepherd do that the psalm talks about?

check.q: In Psalm 23, God is like a what?
check.why: Psalm 23 begins, "The LORD is my shepherd." The whole psalm is about being cared for like a sheep.

check.q: What does the psalm say about the dark valley?
check.why: The psalm says the singer walks through the dark valley and is not afraid.

check.q: Which of these is in Psalm 23?
check.why: Psalm 23 talks about green grass and quiet water. The fish is in Jonah, and the lions are in Daniel.

lessons.title: Daniel and the Lions
lessons.mainIdea: The story says Daniel kept praying, was thrown to the lions, and came out safe.
reading: The book of Daniel tells about a man named *Daniel*. He lived far from home in a city called Babylon. He worked for the king. The story says he was wise and honest.
Some men did not like Daniel. They got the king to make a rule. For thirty days, nobody could pray to anyone but the king. Daniel prayed to God anyway. He prayed three times a day, like always.
So Daniel was thrown into a den of lions. The king was sad all night. In the morning, the story says Daniel was safe. He said God sent an angel to shut the lions' mouths.

words.d: a man in the Bible who the story says was thrown to lions and came out safe
to talk to God

look.title: What Daniel Told the King
look.text: In the morning the king ran to the den. He called out, "Daniel, did your God save you?" The story says Daniel answered: My God sent his angel. The angel shut the lions' mouths. They did not hurt me.
look.cite: Daniel 6:19–22, King James Version (1611), told in simple words
look.prompt: Daniel knew the rule and prayed anyway. Was that brave, or something else? What do you think?

check.q: Why was Daniel thrown to the lions?
check.why: The story says a new rule said not to pray to anyone but the king. Daniel prayed to God anyway.

check.q: How did the story say Daniel stayed safe?
choices: An angel shut the lions' mouths
check.why: Daniel tells the king that God sent an angel to shut the lions' mouths.

check.q: Where did Daniel live?
check.why: The book of Daniel says Daniel lived in Babylon and worked for the king there.

lessons.title: Jonah and the Big Fish
lessons.mainIdea: The story says Jonah ran the wrong way, a big fish swallowed him, and then a whole city said sorry.
reading: The book of Jonah is a short story. The story says God told Jonah to go to a big city called Nineveh. He was to tell the people to stop doing wrong. Jonah did not want to go. He got on a boat going the other way.

A big storm came. The story says Jonah told the sailors to throw him into the sea. They did. Then a big fish swallowed him. Jonah was inside the fish for three days. He prayed. Then the fish spit him out.

This time Jonah went to Nineveh. He told the people his message. The story says the whole city said sorry and changed. Even the king put on rough clothes. And the story says God did not punish the city.

words.d: a man in the Bible who the story says was swallowed by a big fish
the big city the story says Jonah was sent to

look.title: Inside the Fish
look.text: Picture this. It is dark and wet. You hear water moving. You are inside a very big fish. You have been there for three days. The story says Jonah prayed there. Then the fish opened its mouth, and Jonah was on dry land.
look.prompt: What do you think Jonah was thinking inside the fish? What would you do first when you got out?

check.q: Where did the story say Jonah was told to go?
check.why: The story says God sent Jonah to the big city of Nineveh.

check.q: What did Jonah do first?
choices: He got on a boat the other way
check.why: The story says Jonah did not want to go, so he got on a boat going the other way.

check.q: What did the people of Nineveh do?
choices: They threw Jonah in the sea
check.why: The story says the whole city said sorry and changed, even the king.

lessons.title: What a Prophet Is
lessons.mainIdea: In the Bible, a prophet is a person who speaks a message, and speaking it takes courage.
reading: The Bible calls some people prophets. A *prophet* is a person who speaks a message. The Bible says the message comes from God. Jonah was a prophet. Samuel was a prophet too.
A prophet's job was not easy. The message was often hard to hear. Kings and crowds did not always want to listen. Jonah ran away at first. Then he went and spoke anyway.
David, Daniel and Jonah all had to be brave. Being *brave* does not mean you are never scared. It means you do the right thing even when you are scared. Which story shows that best to you?

words.d: a person in the Bible who speaks a message the text says comes from God
doing the right thing even when you feel scared

look.title: Numbers in the Stories
rows: Days Jonah was in the fish
look.cite: 1 Samuel 17:40; Daniel 6:10; Jonah 1:17; Jonah 3:4, King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: Which two numbers are the same? Which story does each number come from?

check.q: What is a prophet?
choices: A person who speaks a message
check.why: In the Bible, a prophet is someone who speaks a message the text says comes from God.

check.q: Which of these was a prophet?
check.why: Jonah was a prophet. The story says he was sent with a message to Nineveh.

check.q: What does being brave mean in this lesson?
choices: Doing the right thing even when scared
check.why: Brave means you do the right thing even when you feel scared, like Daniel and Jonah.

review.q: What did David do before he was king?
review.why: The story says David was a shepherd boy in Bethlehem.

review.q: Who did David fight with a sling?
review.why: The story says David beat the giant Goliath with a sling and a stone.

review.q: What is the book of Psalms full of?
review.why: The book of Psalms has 150 songs and poems.

review.q: Who was thrown to the lions?
review.why: The book of Daniel says Daniel was thrown into a den of lions for praying.
The book of Jonah says a big fish swallowed Jonah for three days.

review.q: Which word means a person who speaks a message?
review.why: A prophet speaks a message. Jonah and Samuel were prophets in the Bible.

chapters.title: Stories Jesus Told
chapters.bigQuestion: Why did Jesus teach with stories, and what do Christians remember about him?

story.title: The One Who Stopped
story.kicker: A man is hurt on the side of the road, and two people walk right past him.
paragraphs: A man is walking down a rocky road. Robbers jump out. They take his money and his clothes. They hit him and leave him on the ground. He cannot get up.
A priest walks by. He sees the hurt man. He crosses to the other side of the road. He keeps going. A helper from the temple walks by next. He looks. He keeps going too.

Then a man from Samaria comes along. People from his town and the hurt man's town did not get along. But he stops. He cleans the man's cuts. He puts him on his own donkey. He takes him to an inn and pays for his bed.
Jesus told this story to answer a question. A man had asked him, "Who is my neighbor?" When the story was done, Jesus asked him back, "Which one was a neighbor to the hurt man?"
story.think: Two people walked past. One stopped. Why do you think Jesus made the helper someone nobody expected?

lessons.title: The Christian Bible and Jesus
lessons.mainIdea: The New Testament is the part of the Bible that Christians read for the story of Jesus.
reading: The Christian Bible has two parts. The first part is the Old Testament. It has the stories of David, Daniel and Jonah. The second part is the *New Testament*. It tells about a teacher named *Jesus*.
Four books tell the story of Jesus. They are called Gospels. Their names are Matthew, Mark, Luke and John. Each one tells the story a little differently.
Christians believe Jesus is the Son of God. Jews and Muslims do not believe that. Muslims honor Jesus as a prophet. In this class we read the stories and learn what people believe.

words.d: the second part of the Christian Bible, which tells about Jesus
the teacher the New Testament is about; Christians believe he is the Son of God
one of four books that tell the story of Jesus

look.title: Books That Tell About Jesus
rows: Gospels that tell about his birth
Gospels that tell the Good Samaritan story
Books in the whole New Testament
look.cite: The New Testament, King James Version (1611); Matthew 1–2, Luke 2, Luke 10
look.prompt: How many Gospels are there? Which number is the biggest?

check.q: Which part of the Bible tells about Jesus?
check.why: The New Testament is the second part of the Christian Bible. It tells about Jesus.

check.q: What is a Gospel?
choices: A book that tells the story of Jesus
check.why: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John are the four Gospels. Each tells the story of Jesus.

check.q: Who believes Jesus is the Son of God?
check.why: Christians believe this. Jews and Muslims do not, though Muslims honor Jesus as a prophet.

lessons.title: Shepherds in the Night
lessons.mainIdea: Luke's Gospel says Jesus was born in Bethlehem and shepherds came to see him.
reading: The Gospel of Luke tells how Jesus was born. His mother was *Mary*. She and Joseph went to the town of Bethlehem. That is the same town where David grew up. There was no room at the inn.
The story says the baby was born and laid in a *manger*. A manger is a box that holds food for animals. That night, shepherds were out. They were watching their sheep.
The story says an angel came to the shepherds. The angel said a baby was born in Bethlehem. Then the sky was full of angels singing. The shepherds ran to town and found the baby.

words.d: the mother of Jesus in the Gospels
a box that holds food for animals; the story says the baby Jesus was laid in one

look.title: What the Angel Said
look.text: The story says the shepherds were very afraid. The angel told them: Do not be afraid. I bring you good news that will make everyone happy. Today a baby is born in David's town. You will find him wrapped up and lying in a manger.
look.cite: Luke 2:8–12, King James Version (1611), told in simple words
look.prompt: The angel says "David's town." Which town is that? Who else in this unit came from there?

check.q: Where does Luke say Jesus was born?
check.why: Luke's Gospel says Mary and Joseph went to Bethlehem, and the baby was born there.

check.q: What is a manger?
choices: A box that holds food for animals
check.why: A manger holds food for animals. The story says the baby was laid in one.

check.q: Who did the angel talk to in Luke's story?
check.why: Luke says the angel came to shepherds who were watching their sheep at night.

lessons.title: A Star and Some Gifts
lessons.mainIdea: Matthew's Gospel tells about wise men who followed a star to bring gifts to Jesus.
reading: The Gospel of Matthew tells the birth story a different way. It does not have shepherds. Instead, it has *wise men* from a land far to the east. They saw a new star in the sky.
The story says the wise men followed the star. They came to Bethlehem. They found the child with his mother Mary. They bowed down. Then they gave him gifts: gold, frankincense and myrrh.
Frankincense and myrrh are sweet-smelling things from trees. They cost a lot. The story does not say how many wise men came. Many people say three, because there were three gifts.

words.d: visitors from the east who Matthew says followed a star to find Jesus
the light in the sky that the story says led the wise men

look.title: Two Tellings of One Birth
look.text: Luke's story has shepherds, an angel and a manger. Matthew's story has wise men, a star and three gifts. Both say the baby was born in Bethlehem. Both say his mother was Mary. Many Christmas pictures put the two stories together in one scene.
look.prompt: What is the same in both stories? What is different? Why might two writers tell it differently?

check.q: Which Gospel tells about the wise men?
check.why: Matthew's Gospel has the wise men and the star. Luke's has the shepherds.

check.q: What led the wise men to Bethlehem?
check.why: Matthew says the wise men saw a star and followed it.

check.q: How many wise men does the story say there were?
check.why: Matthew does not give a number. People say three because there were three gifts.

lessons.title: What a Parable Is
lessons.mainIdea: A parable is a short story with a lesson inside, and the Gospels say Jesus told many of them.
reading: When Jesus grew up, he became a teacher. He walked from town to town. Crowds came to hear him. The Gospels say he often taught with stories. These stories are called *parables*.
A parable is a short story with a lesson inside. It is about everyday things. A lost sheep. A tiny seed. A man on a road. People listen to the story and then think about what it means.
Here is one. A shepherd has one hundred sheep. One gets lost. The story says the shepherd leaves the ninety-nine and looks for the one. When he finds it, he is so happy. He carries it home.

words.d: a short story with a lesson inside
a parable about a shepherd who looks for the one sheep that got lost

look.title: The Lost Sheep, Told Simply
look.text: Jesus asked: If one of you had one hundred sheep and lost one, what would you do? Would you not leave the ninety-nine and go look for the lost one? And when you found it, would you not carry it home on your shoulders, full of joy?
look.cite: Luke 15:3–6, King James Version (1611), told in simple words
look.prompt: The shepherd is happiest about one sheep, not ninety-nine. What do you think the story is trying to say?

check.q: What is a parable?
choices: A short story with a lesson inside
check.why: A parable is a short story with a lesson inside. The Gospels say Jesus told many.

check.q: How many sheep did the shepherd have in the parable?
check.why: The parable says the shepherd had one hundred sheep and one got lost.

check.q: What did the shepherd do when a sheep got lost?
choices: He went to look for it
check.why: The story says the shepherd left the ninety-nine and looked for the lost one.

lessons.title: The Good Samaritan
lessons.mainIdea: In the Good Samaritan story, a neighbor is anyone who stops to help.
reading: This parable is in the Gospel of Luke. A man asked Jesus, "Who is my *neighbor*?" A neighbor is a person near you who you should care about. Jesus did not just give an answer. He told a story.
A man was hurt by robbers. A priest walked by. A temple helper walked by. Neither one stopped. Then a man from Samaria stopped. He is the *Samaritan*. He cleaned the man's cuts and paid for his care.
Then Jesus asked, "Which one was a neighbor?" The man said, "The one who helped." Jesus said, "Go and do the same." Many people still call a helper a good Samaritan today.

words.d: a person near you who you should care about
a person from Samaria; in the parable, the one who stopped to help

look.title: On the Playground
look.text: Picture a playground. A boy trips and falls. His knee is bleeding. Two kids see him and keep playing. Then a girl he has never played with walks over. She helps him up and takes him to the teacher.
look.prompt: Who was a neighbor in this picture? How is it like the story Jesus told?

check.q: Which Gospel has the Good Samaritan story?
check.why: The Good Samaritan parable is in the Gospel of Luke, chapter 10.

check.q: Who stopped to help the hurt man?
check.why: The priest and the temple helper walked past. The Samaritan stopped and helped.

check.q: What question was Jesus answering with this story?
check.why: A man asked Jesus, "Who is my neighbor?" Jesus answered with the story.

lessons.title: The Mustard Seed
lessons.mainIdea: The mustard seed parable says something very small can grow very big.
reading: Jesus told a parable about a *mustard seed*. A mustard seed is tiny. You can hold many of them on one fingertip. The story says it is one of the smallest seeds a farmer plants.
But when it is planted, it grows. The story says it becomes a big plant, like a tree. Birds come and make nests in its branches. Something tiny becomes something big.
Jesus said this is what God's *kingdom* is like. Christians read this in different ways. Many say it means good things can start small and grow. This parable is in Matthew, Mark and Luke.

words.d: a tiny seed that grows into a big plant; the point of one of Jesus's parables
the land a king rules; Jesus used the word for what God's rule is like

look.title: Small Seed, Big Plant
look.text: Look at your fingertip. Now picture a seed so small that ten of them fit on it. Put it in the dirt. Give it sun and water. Weeks go by. Now picture a plant taller than you, with birds sitting in its branches.
look.prompt: What is something small you have seen grow big? Why might Jesus tell a story about a seed?

check.q: What is special about a mustard seed?
check.why: The parable says the mustard seed is one of the smallest seeds, but it grows big.

check.q: What comes to live in the grown plant?
check.why: The story says birds come and nest in the plant's branches.

check.q: What did Jesus say the seed story is like?
check.why: Jesus said the kingdom of God is like a mustard seed that starts small and grows.

lessons.title: Jesus Welcomes Children
lessons.mainIdea: The Gospels say that when helpers tried to send children away, Jesus called them to him.
reading: One day, people brought their children to Jesus. They wanted him to bless them. The Gospel of Mark says his helpers, called *disciples*, told the people to go away. They thought Jesus was too busy.
The story says Jesus was not happy about that. He said, "Let the children come to me." He said God's kingdom is for people like them. He held the children. He blessed them.
Christians often tell this story to kids. It says children matter. In many churches, there are pictures of Jesus with children around him.

words.d: the helpers and students who followed Jesus
to ask for good things for someone

look.title: Let Them Come
look.text: People brought little children to Jesus so he could touch them. The disciples told them to stop. The story says Jesus saw this and was upset. He said: Let the little children come to me. Do not stop them. Then he took the children in his arms and blessed them.
look.cite: Mark 10:13–16, King James Version (1611), told in simple words
look.prompt: The disciples said no. Jesus said yes. Why do you think this story is a favorite for kids?

check.q: Who tried to send the children away?

lessons.title: Christmas and Easter
lessons.mainIdea: Christmas and Easter are days when Christians remember the birth of Jesus and, as they believe, his rising.
reading: *Christmas* is the day Christians remember the birth of Jesus. Most celebrate it on December 25. They tell the story of the manger, the shepherds and the star. Many go to church and sing.
*Easter* comes in the spring. The Gospels say Jesus was killed on a cross. Christians believe that three days later he rose from the dead. Easter is the Sunday when they remember that.

Not everyone celebrates these days. Jewish families have their own holidays, like Passover. Muslim families have Eid. In Chicago, you can see churches, synagogues and mosques in the same neighborhood.

words.d: the day Christians remember the birth of Jesus
the spring Sunday when Christians remember what they believe is Jesus rising from the dead

look.title: Two Days, Two Stories
look.text: Christmas: a baby, a manger, shepherds, a star, songs in the night. Easter: a cross, a garden, an empty tomb, and Christians saying he is alive. One day is about a beginning. One day is about what Christians believe was not the end.

check.q: What do Christians remember on Christmas?
check.why: Christmas is the day Christians remember the birth of Jesus.

check.q: What do Christians believe happened at Easter?
check.why: Christians believe Jesus rose from the dead three days after he died on a cross.

check.why: Passover is a Jewish holiday. Christmas and Easter are Christian holidays.
